messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert fired: PD#98765 — high DB connection utilization (pg-main) + Redis accept queue rising
Alex R: got the page, looking now. seeing steady 100% active DB connections on pgbouncer.
Maria G: Redis maxclients creeping up too, a lot of short-lived spikes from job-runner tasks. could be a churn pattern.
Jamal S: linking metrics: http://grafana/internal/d/DB?orgId=1&var-host=pg-main (ps: read-only replica looks fine) :eyes:
metrics-bot: Current metrics snapshot — pg-main active connections 550/550, pg-replica 120/500, redis-acceptqueue avg 45, redis-maxclients 10240/10240, p50 latency pg 45ms -> 1.2s for tail.
Alex R: root cause hypothesis: nightly analytics job started by a customer triggered a large batch of writes, long-running transactions holding connections, and a cascade of retries from services -> redis accept queue overflow.
Priya (SRE): @Alex R @Maria G escalate to senior? PagerDuty auto-escalation in 2m. Ack?
Alex R: acking oncall. Taking ownership for DB side.
pagerduty: PD#98765 acknowledged by Alex R
Maria G: I'm on Redis. Initial plan: enable short-term ingress throttling on the worker pool for 60s, drop retries at the gateway, and clear stale Redis clients. Can someone flip the feature flag for async-uploads?
Tom - Solutions: I can flip the flag and notify affected tenants. Will do a 5% ramp down, then 50% if still noisy.
Jamal S: running quick psql to see active queries:
```
SELECT pid, usename, state, query_start, now() - query_start AS runtime, query
FROM pg_stat_activity
WHERE state <> 'idle'
ORDER BY runtime DESC
LIMIT 10;
```
Alex R: top ones are `COPY` and `bulk_insert` ops from job-runner-5, holding >8m. Also a few stuck `vacuum` workers.
Alex R: I'm killing the top 3 long-running client sessions now (SIGTERM on backend pid). Will watch for rollback cost.
Maria G: restarted a handful of Redis clients on gateways and bumped `maxclients` on the redis cluster to a soft-limit +200 to buy time (non-persistent nodes).
Priya (SRE): Be careful on bump — risk of OOM on Redis hosts. What's memory headroom?
metrics-bot: Redis memory headroom on affected nodes ~18% free, may run out if we keep increasing.
Alex R: ok rolled back the pids, some queries are rolling back — we saw immediate drop in active connections to ~420.
Tom - Solutions: started feature-flag ramp to 20% (ingestion throttle). Logging tenant impact to support.
Jamal S: Redis acceptqueue down to 12 and redis-maxclients back to 9800. p50 latency improving.
Maria G: removing retries on inbound worker queue via env toggle `WORKER_RETRY_BACKOFF=0` for a minute.
Alex R: switching pgbouncer to transaction pooling for short-lived clients (command below) — will need a reload:
```
echo 'pool_mode = transaction' >> /etc/pgbouncer/pgbouncer.ini
systemctl reload pgbouncer
```
Priya (SRE): That helps if clients are well-behaved. Watch connection reuse.
Alex R: reload succeeded. Active connections dropping to 300, graceful degradation of tail latency.
Jamal S: observing increased queueing on some app pods as they get rate-limited. Latency for user-facing reads still within SLO for now.
Tom - Solutions: support notified tenants WIP; one customer reported slower dashboard loads but no errors. Recording for postmortem.
Priya (SRE): next steps: 1) keep ingest throttle until jobs finish; 2) run a short pg_repack on vacuum backlog overnight; 3) review job-runner scheduling to avoid simultaneous big batches; 4) follow up with customer to coordinate their large job.
Alex R: agree. Creating a quick runbook note: `pg: kill runaway copy -> switch pgbouncer pool_mode -> throttle ingestion -> notify customers -> monitor`
Maria G: I'll open a PR to add backpressure at the worker gateway and a circuit breaker to avoid retry storms.
Tom - Solutions: coordinating a tenant call in 30m to prevent future midnight bursts.
pagerduty: PD#98765 status: Investigating -> Mitigated by Alex R
Alex R: marking for handoff to daytime oncall in 10m. Leaving detailed notes and commands in the incident doc: https://confluence/internal/incidents/PD98765
Priya (SRE): handing off to daytime oncall @dayteam. Please pick up: keep throttles, monitor pg rollback lag, and schedule postmortem with customer.
Alex R: handoff complete. last check: redis acceptqueue 4, pg active connections 165/550, tail latency 180ms. We'll follow up in a postmortem. :white_check_mark:
metrics-bot: Snapshot at end-of-thread: pg_active 165, pg_replica_lag 0.8s, redis_acceptqueue 4, error rate 0.2% (normal).
Tom - Solutions: filing customer impact note and watching support tickets.
Maria G: closing our temporary toggles in 40m unless we see recurrence. Good job team. :tada:
